_help: World, history and everyday facts (personality/knowledge.py). Nothing that changes with the news.

entries.a: A normal year has three hundred and sixty five days, and a leap year has three hundred and sixty six.
Seven days in a week.
Twelve months in a year.
Fifty two weeks in a year.
Sixty minutes in an hour.
Sixty seconds in a minute.
Three thousand six hundred seconds in an hour.
Eighty six thousand four hundred seconds in a day.
A leap year has an extra day, the twenty ninth of February, to keep the calendar in step with Earth's orbit. It comes round every four years, with a few exceptions.
There are twenty six letters in the English alphabet.
Eleven players per side in football, soccer to some of you.
Five players per side on court in basketball.
Five rings in the Olympic symbol, for the five inhabited continents.
A standard guitar has six strings.
A full piano has eighty eight keys.
Three: red, amber and green.
A stop sign has eight sides.
The First World War began in 1914 and ended in 1918.
The Second World War ran from 1939 to 1945.
Alexander Graham Bell is usually credited with inventing the telephone, in 1876.
Thomas Edison made the first practical light bulb, though others worked on the idea before him.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.
Many people built it. The early network ARPANET appeared in the late 1960s, and Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn designed the key protocols.
William Shakespeare, the English playwright who lived from 1564 to 1616.
Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, in the early 1500s.
Isaac Newton described gravity in the 1600s. The apple story may be a little embellished.
Albert Einstein was the physicist behind the theory of relativity, which describes gravity, space and time. He also explained E equals M C squared.
Isaac Newton was an English scientist who worked out the laws of motion and gravity.
Stephen Hawking was a British physicist famous for his work on black holes and the origin of the universe.
Marie Curie was a physicist and chemist who discovered radium and polonium, and won two Nobel Prizes.
Galileo was an Italian astronomer who used a telescope in the early 1600s to show that Jupiter has moons and Earth orbits the Sun.
Carl Sagan was an American astronomer and writer who made space science famous, in books and the series Cosmos.
Napoleon Bonaparte was a French general who became emperor of France in 1804.
Cleopatra was the last active pharaoh of ancient Egypt, who ruled until 30 BC.
The Titanic sank on the fifteenth of April 1912 after hitting an iceberg.
The first Moon landing was on the twentieth of July 1969.
The Japanese currency is the yen.
The pound sterling.
The euro is used by twenty countries, including Germany, France, Italy and Spain.
The US dollar.
Portuguese is spoken in Brazil.
German is the official language of Austria.
Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
English has the most speakers overall, counting people who speak it as a second language. Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers.
There are 195 countries recognised in the world today: 193 United Nations members plus two observer states.
Fifty states in the United States.
Hard to be sure, but Sumerian and Egyptian are among the oldest written languages, and Tamil and Greek are among the oldest still spoken.
George Washington.
The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, France.
Big Ben is in London, at the Houses of Parliament.
The Statue of Liberty stands in New York Harbor.
The great pyramids are at Giza, near Cairo in Egypt.
The Great Wall is in northern China.
The Taj Mahal is in Agra, India.
Machu Picchu is in the Andes mountains of Peru.
Mount Fuji is on the island of Honshu in Japan.
The Kremlin is in Moscow.
The Brandenburg Gate is in Berlin, Germany.
The Colosseum is in Rome, Italy.
In Sydney, Australia.
Oktoberfest is a huge beer festival held in Munich, Germany, starting in late September.
